newsitem.title: GERMANY: German stocks open bourse down, but seen steady.
newsitem.headline: German stocks open bourse down, but seen steady.

text.p: The German DAX index of 30 leading shares opened floor trade lower on Thursday, catching up with losses posted during Wednesday's late electronic trade.

But dealers said the index was well-supported and said they expected it to gradually recover from the blow dealt to it on Wednesday, when shares in one of its leading components, business software firm SAP AG, tumbled on a profit warning.

The DAX was down 15.10 points at 2,684.43, mirroring a drop during post-bourse IBIS electronic trade on Wednesday, triggered after comments by German central bank chief economist Otmar Issing put a dampener on hopes of a further interest rate easing, pushing German bonds down.
Although the Bundesbank is meeting on Thursday, no rate cut is expected by the market.
Dealers said Wednesday's downward correction would only have a temporary effect and could actually have been healthy for the market as a whole.
"Yesterday did some good from the consolidation point of view. It took some of the overheating out of the market. We'll see if we can go in the other direction now," said one dealer.
"In about three or four days we should slowly build up strength to go over the 2,700 point level again," he said.
SAP preference shares, which had tumbled 23 percent on Wednesday, recovered some ground to trade up 6.30 marks at 218.30 marks in bourse trade.
Deutsche Bank also moved against the market trend, gaining 23 pfennigs to 71.80 marks, after it said its net profit in the nine months to September 30 had risen nine percent to 1.53 billion marks.

Engineering group MAN AG was the morning's biggest faller on the DAX, dropping 13.80 marks, or 3.4 percent, to 387 marks, after its truck making unit MAN Nutzfahrzeuge said it expected 1996/97 sales to fall six percent and output to decline 10 percent.
